links.outcome: Predialysis serum potassium and hyperkalemia proportion after GPT-based versus conventional dietary education
links.effect: Serum potassium 4.57 ± 0.76 vs 4.84 ± 0.94 mmol/L (P = .004); hyperkalemia fell from 39.8% to 25% (P = .036). Sequential before-after design, not randomized.
links.quote: Importantly, compared to traditional dietary education, dietary education based on the GPTs tool reduced the proportion of hyperkalemia in HD patients from 39.8% to 25% (P = .036).

screen.reason: Evaluates the clinical impact and accuracy of a patient-facing GPT-based dietary recommendation tool on serum potassium levels in hemodialysis patients, but evaluates the system overall rather than testing a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
